title: Shutdown cancels the flush loop mid-ship; the popped batch is not re-queued on cancel
diff: batches. Losing audit events is a compliance problem, so the buffer
+                # A failed ship must not kill the loop; events stay
+                # local and the next tick retries.
+            # Ship may or may not have landed; re-queue so nothing is
+            # dropped (the audit service dedupes by event id).
+        """Stop the loop, then drain whatever is left."""
+Deploys send SIGTERM and wait up to 30s; every component's aclose()
+must finish inside that budget, so shutdown runs them concurrently.

ground_truth.explanation: _flush_once() pops up to MAX_BATCH events out of the buffer BEFORE awaiting the ship call. The new timeout handling carefully re-queues the batch on TimeoutError -- but aclose() cancels the flush loop, and if the cancellation lands while _flush_once() is suspended inside the awaited ship, CancelledError (which is not an Exception and passes both handlers) propagates without re-queueing: the popped batch of up to 100 audit events vanishes. aclose()'s subsequent drain loop then flushes only what is still IN the buffer, so shutdown looks successful. The bug requires reasoning about a multi-step interleaving -- pop, suspend at await, cancel arrives, which except clauses match -- and it hides behind a diff that visibly ADDS a re-queue path for the timeout case. The tests cover batching, timeout re-queue and a drain where cancellation lands during the sleep (the common timing), never during an in-flight ship.\n\nOffline validation (execution_validated): a standalone asyncio reproduction that cancels aclose-style during an in-flight ship lost the entire popped batch in every trial; the same scenario with a CancelledError re-queue handler lost nothing. Counts are in the validation note.
ground_truth.validation_note: Standalone asyncio reproduction: cancellation landing during the awaited ship, without a CancelledError requeue handler, lost events in 50/50 trials; the same scenario with a CancelledError requeue lost events in 0/50. Script and raw output preserved as private provenance, not in this repository.
